name: radio-group
title: Radio Group
description: A set of checkable buttons—known as radio buttons—where no more than one of the buttons can be checked at a time.
usageSnippet:
<let/selected=("option-one" as string | null)/>

<RadioGroup items=[{ value: "option-one", label: "Option One" }, { value: "option-two", label: "Option Two" }] value:=selected/>

props.name: defaultValue
props.description:
The initial value of the checked radio when rendered.
Use when you don't need to control the value of the radio group.

props.name: disabled
props.description: If `true`, the radio group will be disabled

props.name: form
props.description: The associate form of the underlying input.

props.name: getRootNode
props.description: A root node to correctly resolve document in custom environments. E.x.: Iframes, Electron.

props.name: ids
props.description: The ids of the elements in the radio. Useful for composition.

props.name: invalid
props.description: If `true`, the radio group is marked as invalid.

props.name: name
props.description:
The name of the input fields in the radio
(Useful for form submission).

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether the radio group is read-only

props.name: required
props.description: If `true`, the radio group is marked as required.

events.name: onValueChange
events.description: Function called once a radio is checked

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: Pass an `items: { value, label, disabled? }[]` array and the component renders every item internally — or compose options in markup with `<@item>` attribute tags (see the Compound example).

examples.title: Fieldset
examples.description: Wrap `RadioGroup` in `FieldSet`/`FieldLegend`/`FieldDescription` to group items with a label and description. Upstream additionally wraps each item in its own `<Field orientation="horizontal">`; our items already render an equivalent label+control pairing internally, so only the outer fieldset composition is needed.

examples.title: Disabled item
examples.description: Set `disabled` on a single item to remove it from the tab order and ignore pointer input.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.description: Pass `disabled` on `RadioGroup` itself to disable every item in the group.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.source:
import RadioGroup from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/radio-group/radio-group.marko"; static const ITEMS = [ { value: "default", label: "Default" }, { value: "comfortable", label: "Comfortable" }, { value: "compact", label: "Compact" }, ];
{ value = next; } /> value: ${value ?? "none"}
examples.description: Zag machines are controlled: a `value` prop without a change handler never moves. Pair it with `valueChange`, or use Marko's bind shorthand `value:=state`.

examples.title: Compound (attr tags)
examples.source:
import RadioGroup from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/radio-group/radio-group.marko";

<RadioGroup defaultValue="comfortable">
  <@item value="default">Default</@item>
  <@item value="comfortable">Comfortable</@item>
  <@item value="compact" disabled>Compact</@item>
</RadioGroup>
examples.description: Use `<@item>` attribute tags instead of `items=` to compose each option directly in markup.

examples.title: RTL
examples.description: `dir` isn't a @zag-js/radio-group machine prop, so it passes through as a native attribute on the root — pair it with logical-property CSS for full mirroring.

composition:
RadioGroup
├── item (from `items=`, or an `<@item>` attribute tag)
